rows.question: If I work extra hours, can I get them back as time off?
rows.answer: Where your manager has approved in advance that you work more than 40 hours in a week, you may record the additional hours as time off in lieu (TOIL). [1]

rows.question: How long is the probation period for new hires?
rows.answer: All new employees complete a probationary period of six months. [1] After probation, the notice period you must give is one month for employees below Senior grade and three months for employees at Senior grade and above. [2] During probation, new starters are expected to work from the office at least three days per week so they can get to know their team. [3]

rows.question: What notice do I need to give if I quit during probation?
rows.answer: After probation, the notice period you must give is one month for employees below Senior grade and three months for employees at Senior grade and above. [1] During probation, either party may end employment by giving one week's notice. [2]

rows.question: Which day of the month do we get paid?
rows.answer: Salaries are paid monthly by bank transfer on the 25th of each month. [1] If the 25th falls on a weekend or bank holiday, you will be paid on the last working day before it. [1]

rows.question: How much does Halden put into my pension?
rows.answer: Halden auto-enrols eligible employees into the company pension scheme. [1] Halden pays up to three days of emergency dependant leave per calendar year at full pay; further time off is unpaid. [3]

rows.question: When do salary increases take effect?
rows.answer: Salaries are reviewed once a year, with any changes taking effect from 1 April. [1] After one year of service this increases to 20 working days of full pay. [2]

rows.question: How many holiday days do full-time staff get?
rows.answer: Full-time employees receive 25 days of annual leave per leave year, plus the eight UK bank holidays. [1] After two full years of service, you receive one additional day of leave for each further full year of service, up to a maximum of 30 days. [1] After one year of service this increases to 20 working days of full pay. [4]

rows.question: How many unused holiday days can I roll over to next year?
rows.answer: You may carry over up to five unused days into the next leave year; carried-over days must be used by 31 March or they are lost. [1]

rows.question: By what time should I call in sick?

rows.question: When do I need a doctor's note for sick leave?

rows.question: How many days of full sick pay do I get after my first year?
rows.answer: Company sick pay: during your first year of service you receive full pay for up to 10 working days of sickness in any rolling 12-month period. [1]

rows.question: How often are performance reviews held?
rows.answer: Performance is reviewed twice a year: a mid-year review in October and an annual review in April. [1] Pay reviews take account of performance, market data and the company's financial position. [2]

rows.question: What is the deadline for raising a formal grievance?
rows.answer: Grievances and disciplinary matters. [1] If that is not possible, raise a formal grievance in writing to your manager or the People Team within 20 working days of the issue arising. [1] At any formal grievance or disciplinary meeting you have the right to be accompanied by a colleague or a trade union representative. [1]

rows.question: Can I travel first class on the train?
rows.answer: Rail travel is in standard class. [1] First class is permitted only when the fare is cheaper than standard class, or for journeys over four hours with prior approval from a director. [1]
